pages.title: Deployment and connectivity
pages.lede: Deployment here means the public connectivity wizard: ports for the apps you use, FQDNs for your cluster, then voice. It is not a professional-services statement of work.

p: The wizard tells you to learn ports for the applications you use, then FQDNs and IP addresses for your cluster, then FQDNs and IP addresses for voice.
The same pages say to monitor the connectivity pages because the lists change. This campus does not freeze an allowlist.

The connectivity requirements page defines commercial as the standard environment, FedRAMP as an isolated U.S. federal environment with continuous monitoring and restricted access, and a sovereign cloud as a region that keeps data residency and operations inside a country’s legal boundary.
If you do not know the cluster, the page says to ask the account representative. Do not guess na1.
Select only the applications in the ports checklist that the tenant uses. Copy that result, not this whole table.
Allow paired ranges. The IP address page says a missing range is a failover risk.
Integrated Softphone has its own allowlist, including a separate FedRAMP list, reached through the wizard.
Require TLS 1.2 and at least one listed cipher in each direction before you call the integration done.

pages.title: Migration checklist, not a fake cutover
pages.lede: The public pages this campus uses describe three different moves. They do not publish one ACD replacement cookbook. The checklist keeps those moves apart.

p: Workforce data from Cisco UCCE or Avaya CMS is a WFM connector. The UCCE connector page and the Multi-ACD version table are different products and name different versions.
Live third-party phones recorded into CXone are Multi-ACD. Historical files are Migrated Calls and need the Migrated Interactions Upload license.
Replacing the ACD itself is not a procedure in these pages. Mark that line “ask the account team” instead of inventing weekends and freeze windows.

blocks.h: What you can schedule from the cited pages
p: Confirm the connector version on the connector’s own page. Do not copy the Multi-ACD table onto WFM.
For Migrated Calls, export, merge, and import. Every user needs an email. Screen recordings and digital interactions are not supported.
Vendors named for migrated history include NiCE Engage, CXone, Playback Portal, Uptivity, Verint, Genesys, Calabrio, Witness, Red Box, and Avaya. Anyone else is case by case.
Engage NMF converts to MP4 on playback. Teams are uploaded, not synchronized.
Write the current ACD, the thing that must keep working tomorrow, and which of the three moves you are actually doing.
Book the change against the release calendar only after you re-read the current cycle page. Targeted dates move, and 26.3 and 26.4 overlap on the pages we read.
Leave a blank row called “PBX cutover steps.” If a design review fills it with steps that have no URL, delete them.

pages.title: E911 and emergency calling
pages.lede: An agent with an outbound voice skill can dial an emergency number. A verified address is what sends that call to the local dispatch center. Unverified addresses go to the national center.

p: Set an Emergency Call Notification Email and an Emergency Call Default Callback Phone on the business unit, under Telecom Connectivity.
If Telephone 1 is filled on the agent profile, that number is the callback instead of the business-unit default.

Enter the physical address on the user record and save that individual record. The page says a bulk edit is not enough: each address is verified from the individual save. Look for the green Verified for Emergency Call Dispatching mark.
The agent still needs an outbound phone skill.

blocks.h: What the agent does in MAX
p: US-based agents can type 911. A verified address routes to the local public-safety answering point. Otherwise the call goes to the national emergency center.
933 tests the configuration. The setup page says that test dial is at no additional cost. Real emergency calls may incur charges, and the feature is not available in every country.

blocks.h: What this page will not claim
p: This lab does not list country availability, prices, or a SIP header for emergency calls. Those are account-representative and carrier facts.
Do not treat 933 as a substitute for a real dispatch test plan your own safety team signs.

pages.title: Reporting and analytics
pages.lede: Interaction Analytics (CXone) has prebuilt reports, dashboard widgets, and a JSON export. Dashboard permissions are separate from the widget permissions.

p: The data and reporting page names four prebuilt reports: Analytics Metric Statistics, Analytics Category Statistics, Analytics Metric Comparison, and Analytics Metric Trend.
A short training video is mentioned for the metric and category statistics reports. This campus does not host that video.
The Frustration widget is an Interaction Analytics widget. It needs the Interaction Analytics license plus Analytics > Dashboard Widgets, Dashboard view, and optionally Dashboard edit.
Organizations with a Performance Management (Native) license can see up to 95 days inside a 25-month lookback. A dashboard-only license is limited to same-day data, on that widget page.
If the organization is not configured for Dashboard, or the apps do not include ACD or QM, the dashboard permission page says those permissions will not appear.
Analytics data export writes JSON to a secure external access bucket. Files go out every 400 records or every 6 minutes, whichever comes first.
The page warns that duplicates can exist and that order is processing order, not contact order. Do not build a deduplicated warehouse assumption on top of silence.

pages.title: Security and what the pages actually require
pages.lede: TLS 1.2, a short cipher list, access keys that inherit an employee, and an external IdP if you configure one. This page does not award the tenant a compliance badge the help page did not name.

p: Connectivity in NiCE CXone requires at least TLS 1.2.

Inbound, from CXone to your servers, must support at least one of: TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (0x009E), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA (0xC013), TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (0xC02B), TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (0xC02C).
Outbound, from your servers to CXone, must support at least one of: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (0xC02F) and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 (0xC030). The page recommends both.
An access key belongs to an employee and inherits that employee’s permissions. The secret is shown once. Disabling the key kills tokens.
User-facing apps in this lab follow the authorization-code flow. The authentication pages also show a password grant for back-end integrations, where the username is the access key id.
External IdP is a documented setup, not the default this page assumes you have.

blocks.h: FedRAMP is an environment, not a slogan
p: The connectivity requirements page describes FedRAMP as isolated from commercial operations, with continuous monitoring and restricted access. The API getting-started page names a separate issuer, https://cxone-gov.niceincontact.com.
This campus does not claim HIPAA, PCI, SOC 2, or a particular encryption-at-rest setting. Those sentences are not in the passages gathered here.

pages.title: Licenses the help pages name
pages.lede: A license sentence is a gate. This campus lists gates a cited page states. It does not invent SKUs or prices.

p: CRM Ticketing requires a CRM Ticketing license, and the search permission still matters.
Migrated Calls requires the Migrated Interactions Upload license and the upload permission.
AutoSummary must be enabled with the account representative. Using it with MAX, rather than an agent application, also needs a Copilot for Agents license.
Salesforce CRM integration is billed by how many employees have the Agent Integrations attribute enabled. That is not a public price.
Interaction Analytics widgets require the Interaction Analytics license. Performance Management (Native) changes how much history a widget can show.
Release notes say some features need a purchased license or a public preview signup. From 26.3, Controlled Release is renamed Public Preview.

foundations.title: Foundations and prerequisites
foundations.blurb: Contacts, points of contact, skills, scripts, and the network facts you need before you touch Admin.

lessons.title: What the platform actually routes
lessons.summary: An inbound contact enters through a point of contact. That point of contact names one ACD skill and one Studio script, and the script may choose a more specific skill.
objectives: See where an IVR changes the skill

p: Studio Fundamentals uses four words for the rest of this lab. An ACD skill automates delivery to an agent who is likely to help, using criteria such as department, specialty, language, or location. A channel is the medium a contact uses. A media type is the kind of channel a script is built for, such as phone, chat, or email. A point of contact is the entry, such as a phone number or an email address.

Each point of contact is assigned one ACD skill and one Studio script. Several points of contact may share a skill or a script. The script begins with the point of contact's default skill and can select a more specific skill, for example after a menu.

sections.h: Why the default skill is not the whole story
p: The help page's phone example is the familiar menu: sales, support, or billing. Those spoken choices correspond to ACD skills. If you leave the script without a decision, every contact stays on the single skill that was assigned to the point of contact.
That is the whole inbound contract. Memorize it before you memorize button paths in Admin. The later ACD track walks the clicks. This lesson is the shape those clicks have to produce.

lessons.summary: Help pages use contact for the person and interaction for the full conversation on a channel. Digital is a specific family of channels, not a synonym for every non-voice contact.

figure.caption: Words the help pages actually use

p: On the digital routing page, a contact is the person interacting with an agent, IVR, or bot. An interaction, on the Autopilot page, is the full conversation through a channel: a voice call, email, chat, or social conversation.

Digital, on those same pages, means any channel, contact, or skill associated with Digital Experience. It is not a casual word for 'not a phone call.' Legacy ACD channels such as phone, email, and chat have their own script types. Digital channels share one digital script type.

sections.h: Why the distinction shows up in routing
p: Before the Summer 2023 release, digital contacts were primarily routed with Digital Experience routing queues. New inbound digital routing is configured with digital skills and Studio scripts. Routing queues remain for outbound digital interactions.
If you import a voice habit ('make a queue') into digital inbound work, you are building the pattern the help page tells you to stop creating.

When you create an inbound phone skill, the skill form asks for a campaign. The skill belongs to that campaign. The campaign is not the tenant, and it is not the point of contact.

sections.h: The same tenant shows up in an API token

A multi-tenant app must not hard-code na1. The page says the base URL should be built dynamically per tenant.

lessons.title: Browser, WebRTC, and allowlists

sections.h: The connectivity page draws a hard line
p: If the agent leg is VoIP, NiCE CXone offers two softphone options. Integrated Softphone is built into the platform, so there is nothing to install on the agent computer. Softphone is a separate application that must be installed.

The same page says Integrated Softphone is sometimes called WebRTC, and that the two names do not refer to the same thing. WebRTC is the communications technology available in the Chrome web browser. It is what the application called Integrated Softphone uses.

sections.h: Allowlists and what this lab will not invent
p: The connectivity page says that if you use Integrated Softphone, there are IP addresses that must be added to your allowlist. The page should be opened for the current list. This lab does not copy a list that can change.

PSTN, on that page, is any phone traffic routed via DID or toll-free number. VoIP transports calls over the internet and needs a VoIP phone or a softphone. A SIP trunk is defined there as a virtual connection that lets a PBX communicate with a carrier network, using a phone line, VoIP, or a dedicated connection such as MPLS.

sections.h: Keep the RFC and the product page apart
p: SIP is specified in RFC 3261. That document is the place to learn INVITE, responses, and dialogs. NiCE's connectivity page does not reprint the RFC. It defines a SIP trunk as a virtual connection that allows a PBX to communicate with a carrier network.

The agent leg is a different hop. It is Integrated Softphone or the installable Softphone. Mixing a SIP ladder from the carrier with a WebRTC agent leg is normal in a design, and it is a mistake to draw them as one protocol.

sections.h: What you can say in a design review

When a design needs those values, open the current connectivity and telephony requirements pages and your carrier's build sheet. Mark anything else as unknown.

lessons.title: AHT, service level, and the numbers routing serves
lessons.summary: WFM forecasts volume and average handle time, then you choose a speed-of-answer target. A tighter target needs more agents. Routing features such as bullseye change who is eligible, which can change the forecast.
objectives: Define AHT the way the forecast page does

p: General Forecast says you review historical data, and forecasting predicts volume and average handle time. AHT is defined there as the average length of time to complete a transaction from start to finish. You then decide how the center should perform. The page's example is answering or dialing each call in less than 10 seconds compared with 30 seconds.

Lowering average speed of answer, or increasing dials, needs more agents. The last step is a staffing plan from the staffing parameters and the forecast data. Accurate results need at least three months of history, and the same page also recommends at least 13 weeks.

sections.h: Routing changes the work the forecast assumed

Workforce Management (CXone) and Workforce Management (IEX Integrated) are different products. The bullseye page points CXone WFM users at the online help and IEX users at the Distribution Rules Guide.

lessons.title: How to read a help page and a release note
lessons.summary: Major releases happen four times a year. Dates on the 26.3 and 26.4 pages do not line up cleanly. This lab marks that clash instead of smoothing it over.
objectives: Treat Coming Soon as a plan, not a promise

p: The release process page says a cycle runs from the Coming Soon notes until the release reaches the last customer cluster. Coming Soon notes are published 30 days before deployment to beta clusters. Final release notes and help updates publish on or shortly before beta. Customer clusters start two weeks after beta, a few clusters each week.

Cumulative updates and pipeline updates occur on separate cadences, roughly every three weeks. Hotfixes ship when needed. Features marked 'available later in the release cycle' arrive in an update. The service notification page adds that a major release happens four times a year, and that deployment dates in notifications are not guaranteed.

sections.h: Dates that disagree, left in view
p: The 26.2 notes say that cycle begins on 29 April 2026 and ends when the next release begins, then targeted for 28 July 2026. The 26.3 notes say the cycle was first planned for 3 August 2026 through 25 October 2026, then moved, because of a change moratorium, to 2 September 2026 through 5 November 2026.

The 26.4 Coming Soon page says that cycle begins on 26 October 2026 and the next release is targeted for 4 February 2027. Those 26.3 and 26.4 windows overlap. Both pages say features are subject to change. This lab does not pick a winner.

lessons.title: Access keys are not passwords
lessons.summary: A person logs in with a password or an IdP. A back-end app sends an access key id and secret to the token endpoint. The global token URL comes from OpenID discovery, not from a guess.
objectives: Call discovery before the token URL
Map key id and secret onto the password grant

p: Getting Started says a back-end app provides an access key id and secret. For client_secret_basic, you send a basic authorization header with the application's client id and secret, and a form body with grant_type password, username set to the access key id, and password set to the secret. client_secret_post puts the client id and secret in the body instead.

You learn the token URL from the discovery document. Global production discovery is https://cxone.niceincontact.com/.well-known/openid-configuration. The sample response on the page includes token_endpoint https://cxone.niceincontact.com/auth/token.

The page says the token response includes a TTL, and that you should plan to renew before 5 minutes of access token expiry. It also says expires_in may differ from one token to the next. The sample token body shows expires_in 3600. Treat 3600 as that sample, not a contract.
OpenID Connect, for a user-facing app, is a different flow: scope openid, response_type code, then an authorization code at the token endpoint. Do not paste the password grant into a browser login.

p: The contact calls a local or toll-free number. The call crosses the PSTN and enters CXone. That portion is the A leg, inbound or ingress. CXone queues it for agents with the right skills.

A transfer places a second B leg to the next agent. All three legs meet on the media server, then the first agent drops.
On an outbound call, both legs originate in CXone and are egress. CXone can dial for the agent when that is configured.

lessons.summary: The preferred toll-free path is to make CXone the RespOrg. Local numbers can be ported. Other arrivals are remote call forwarding, an independent carrier, or your PBX. A voice PoP is the carrier's PSTN gateway.
objectives: Define PoP and SIP trunk as the page does

p: The preferred option is to authorize CXone as the Responsible Organization for the toll-free numbers you want to use. Local numbers can be ported if you want that.

Other methods: remote call forwarding, directly from an independent carrier, or directly from your PBX. If CXone is the RespOrg, you order more numbers through CXone. Otherwise you order them from your carrier.
A voice Point of Presence is the physical place your carrier connects to the PSTN. It is the gateway for calls to and from the carrier.

A SIP trunk is a virtual connection from your PBX to the carrier. It can use a traditional phone line, VoIP, or a dedicated connection such as MPLS. RFC 3261 is the SIP protocol. It is not a list of CXone headers.
